title: Honey-Soy Glazed Chicken Rice Bowls
summary: Baked chicken thighs brushed with a honey, soy and Fresno chili glaze, over medium-grain rice with charred broccoli and edamame, quick-pickled carrots and avocado.
notes: Video: 'Easy Chicken Rice Bowls Anyone Can Make' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Written recipe for the same dish: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/easiest-healthy-chicken-bowl-at-home (serves 4, prep 15 min, cook 40 min; servings and times come from it). The video states the rice, water ratio, glaze, broccoli, pickle and carrots. From the written recipe, because the video is unclear: 8 thighs (video: 'six to eight'), cornstarch (garbled in the captions), 8 oz edamame (video: 'half a bag'), 1-2 Tbsp oil (we use 1.5), 1 lemon, 1 large avocado. Our estimates: the salt on the chicken (1 tsp kosher, he says go lighter because of the glaze) and on the vegetables (1/2 tsp). Broccoli is 2 crowns in both; the gram weight of the florets is ours. Pickling liquid, cooking spray, green onion, flaky salt and furikake are not counted (mostly left behind, or no amount). Carrot size ('large') is from the written recipe. The avocado uses USDA's average Hass fruit (136 g edible), so a large one is understated. The Fresno chili is weighed as a jalapeño-sized chili (14 g, USDA jalapeño).

steps.text: Rinse the rice in the rice-cooker bowl 2-3 times, until the water runs mostly clear. Level it, add the water and start the cooker.
Heat the oven to 375°F (convection if you have it). Grease a sheet tray, lay the thighs on it bone side down, spray the tops and season both sides lightly with salt.
Roast the chicken for 30-35 minutes in total.

For the glaze, finely chop the seeded chili. Bring the soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey and chili to a boil over medium-high, boil 1 minute, lower to medium, stir in the cornstarch slurry until thickened, then turn off the heat and stir in the garlic.

Cut the broccoli into florets. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high until nearly smoking, add the broccoli and edamame, salt, and sear without tossing for 2-3 minutes. Toss, lower to medium and cook about 5 minutes more, until the broccoli is crisp-tender. Finish with lemon juice.
About halfway through the roast, brush both sides of the chicken with some of the glaze and return it to the oven.
For the carrots, whisk the vinegar, water, salt and sugar until dissolved. Julienne the carrots (or slice them thin on a mandoline) and toss them in the liquid.
Slice the green onions and the avocado.
Brush the rest of the glaze over the tops of the chicken and broil 1-3 minutes, until caramelized and lightly charred.
Slice the chicken about 1/2 inch thick. Serve over rice with the vegetables, drained carrots, avocado, flaky salt, green onion and furikake.
